column2: Tenant-local copy dedup identity and sink
column6: `crates/module-copy/src/tenant_executor.rs` uses full event identity for local dedup, retries an unavailable shared decision without releasing the remote mark, and excludes duplicate/unavailable outcomes from the tenant sink. `evidence/claim-gate/tenant-copy-dedup-2026-11-09.txt` records the rerun after reconstruction covering distinct mint/side, duplicate sink suppression and unavailable retry using an in-memory test sink. This is not a real PostgreSQL tenant sink or multi-replica test.

(1) PostgreSQL treated expiry as advisory: `DedupRepo::mark` was `ON CONFLICT … DO NOTHING` and `exists` selected on (namespace, key) alone, while `expires_at` was honoured only by `cleanup_expired` on the HOURLY leased worker, so a 60-second window behaved like "up to an hour" depending on when a lease holder ticked. `exists` now filters `expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now()` and `mark` reclaims a lapsed row in the same statement (`DO UPDATE … WHERE expires_at <= now()`), which leaves first-arrival semantics for live rows untouched; cleanup is now pure GC because deleting an expired row cannot change a decision. (2) `RedisKv::set_nx_ttl` clamped `Duration::ZERO` to 1 ms via `.as_millis().max(1)` — the opposite of "no window", it makes every call a first arrival; the primitive now refuses zero before sending any command. (3) the process-local L1 `BoundedSet` had no time notion and outlived the backend TTL for the whole process; it now stamps first-seen `Instant`s and prunes/validates against the window, with zero TTL still the one deliberate indefinite case. A first attempt that cleared the namespace map on every mark was caught by the existing `first_arrival_wins_exactly_once` test and reverted. Witnesses: `db_integration.rs::an_expired_dedup_key_stops_gating_reads_and_marks`, `redis_kv.rs::tests::set_nx_ttl_refuses_a_zero_window_and_honours_a_short_one` (real Redis), `dedup.rs::l1_does_not_outlive_a_nonzero_ttl_window`; four RED runs recorded. GREEN: db_integration 31/31, dedup+redis lib 11/11, clippy/fmt/diff clean. Evidence: `evidence/claim-gate/dedup-ttl-enforcement-2026-11-09.txt`. Residual: no sub-millisecond accuracy claimed (Postgres `now()` is transaction time, Redis PX is millisecond) and no cross-replica clock-skew detection; cleanup still runs hourly, it is simply no longer load-bearing for correctness.

column5: the guard asks the durable binding registry, and factory-built engines carry that check by default
column6: `binding_guard` already refused an inactive/unbound signer at ISSUANCE, but the captured `TenantSignerRef.active` in a running module was never re-read: `authorize_signer` (the only `is_active()` reader) had no caller outside its own tests, so a binding revoked after issuance kept signing until restart. Fixed with the same seam pattern as the runtime fence: new `SignerBindingProbe` trait (`Err` never passes), `with_signer_probe`/`has_signer_probe`, and `authorize_live` now runs captured rules → LIVE binding → runtime fence (a revoked signer refuses before any runtime I/O); new deny `SignerInactive{detail,source}` → `signer_inactive`, deliberately distinct from the captured `SignerRevoked` and from `runtime_fenced`. `LivenessProbes{fence,signer}` + `with_liveness` attach both into the executors; server adapter `RegistrySignerProbe` maps active → pass, inactive → `binding_revoked`, missing → `binding_not_found`, store error → refusal; `TenantModuleFactory` builds BOTH probes itself over its own database (memoised), so nothing depends on a boot step. Witnesses: guard-level (live source consulted once with this tenant's provider/key_ref; revocation ⇒ `signer_inactive` while `authorize_meta` still passes; revoked signer ⇒ ZERO runtime lookups), server adapter over a scripted registry, and real-PostgreSQL end-to-end (factory engine, no opt-in, durable row flipped to inactive ⇒ `SignerInactive{binding_revoked}`). RED: deleting the signer branch fails `the live signer binding must be consulted` (left: 0); detaching the factory probe fails `every factory-built engine must carry a live signer-binding check`. Evidence: `evidence/claim-gate/signer-revocation-at-broadcast-2026-11-09.txt`. Behaviour change: a probe-carrying guard now refuses an unbound key reference (production contexts always have an active row; hand-built fixtures must seed `tenant_bindings`). Residual: the binding's `public_address` is still not compared to the funding wallet at broadcast time (key rotated under the same `key_ref` would need that), `custody_signers` is not consulted by this probe, and the witnesses are paper-mode.

column2: Signing key rotation under an unchanged reference
column5: the guard pins the signer key at build and re-resolves it at broadcast
column6: The revocation check answered a different question than "will the approved key sign?". `tenant_bindings` stores the signer's key REF (not its public address), so a custody rotation that keeps `provider/key_ref` leaves the row active, while the executor signs through its in-process `SignerRegistry`, which resolves an identity to a key at call time — nothing compared the two. Fixed: `with_expected_signer_key` pins the key the executor can actually sign with; `authorize_signer_identity(resolved)` refuses an unregistered identity, a non-pinned key, or a key that does not control the bound wallet; new deny `SignerKeyMismatch` → `signer_key_mismatch` (distinct from captured `signer_revoked` and live `signer_inactive`); `Executor::run` RE-RESOLVES the signer at broadcast and `send_prebuilt` checks already-signed bytes too; both module executors pin at construction when given a registry. The in-process registry is the right authority because signing never fetches a key from the database. Witnesses: guard-level (unregistered / different key / key that is not the bound wallet), end-to-end through `Executor::run` with a `SwitchSigner` that keeps its identity and changes its key, and real-PostgreSQL (active binding row, rotated key refused, engine for the rotated wallet refused at build). RED: checking only the construction-time pin (instead of re-resolving) makes the rotated key produce a PAPER FILL — `left: PaperFilled, right: Skipped`. Evidence: `evidence/claim-gate/signer-key-rotation-2026-11-09.txt`. Residual: wallet-only executors pin nothing beyond the funding wallet (no second key exists), `custody_signers.public_address` is still not consulted, and the witnesses are paper-mode.

column5: reproduced against real PostgreSQL and fixed
column6: `PostgresRiskOracle::realized_pnl_read` summed positions closed inside today's UTC window (`closed_at >= midnight AND closed_at < midnight + 1 day`) but its Polymarket completeness probe asked `poly_fills.ts >= midnight` with no upper bound, so it answered a question about a wider row set than the number it guards. column2: Tenant recovery truncation and lock boundary
column5: the sweep now PAGES, PAIRS and documents its lock boundary. (1) Truncation: `sweep_page` walks a `(created_at, intent_id)` keyset — the full sort key, so rows sharing a timestamp are neither skipped nor repeated — with `RECOVERY_PAGE_MAX = 500`, and returns `has_more`, `total_remaining` and `next_cursor`, so a caller that stops early KNOWS it stopped early; the old `LIMIT 1000`/`LIMIT 5000` with no cursor and no signal was invisible and unreachable past the cap. (2) Pairing: each intent now carries only the non-terminal orders attributed to it (`orders.meta->>'intent_id'`), instead of one tenant-wide list cloned onto every item; open orders with NO attribution are reported as `unattributed_open_order_ids` (tenant-wide, bounded) so nothing is guessed onto an unrelated intent and nothing is silently dropped. (3) Lock boundary: the tenant advisory lock covers the two SELECTs only and is released at commit, which is now stated as the contract — it serializes two workers' reads, while each decision is re-fenced by `abandon_orphan`/`link_orphan` (both only transition a still-`pending` row), so holding it across the caller's processing would add unbounded blocking without adding safety. The API (`GET /api/tenant/recovery/sweep`) accepts `limit`/`before`/`before_id` (a half keyset is a 422) and returns `has_more`/`total_remaining`/`next_before`/`next_before_id`/`unattributed_open_order_ids`; OpenAPI (json + yaml) and the control-plane TS type were regenerated. column5: a stale replica posts the sell at the COMMITTED cost, and the only `#[ignore]` in `crates/` is gone
column6: The defect was real and reproduced: `submit` priced a sell from the replica's LOCAL book, so a replica that never saw the opening buy posted inventory credit `0` and booked the entire proceeds as realized PnL (witness failed with `got -0` against `-0.5`). Fixed by pricing from what the journal COMMITTED: `committed_slice_cost` detects that the local book does not cover the position's history (or has nothing applied for it) and delegates to `journal_slice_cost`, which replays the position's committed events in journal order and applies them from their RECORDED POSTINGS via the new `PositionBook::apply_committed` — inventory movement and realized result come from the entry, so a replica that never saw the buy books the same cost. Cash-only events delegate to `apply`. Plumbing: new `LedgerStore::load_entry(&event_id) -> Option<Option<Entry>>` (conservative default), implemented for `MemoryLedgerStore` and over `ledger_postings` for the server's `DbLedgerStore` (`AccountingRepo::load_entry`, `ORDER BY seq`). `submit` and `hydrate` share the code, so live and replay agree. No schema change — the committed amounts were already stored. Fail-closed: journal unavailable / undecodable posting / invalid history row ⇒ the local cost is used and a `warn!` names the event; a missing cost is never silently zero. Evidence `evidence/claim-gate/stale-replica-committed-cost-2026-11-09.txt`. GREEN: the former `#[ignore]` test now runs (1/1), core accounting 59/59, `global_risk_accounting` 29/29, `accounting_retry_postgres` 1/1 on real PostgreSQL, server accounting 1/1.
